summary: F1 and F2 are fixed. The program grid remains unbalanced at 980 and 1280 pixels. F3 blocks the PM look check. All 18 automated browser checks pass.
blocking_findings: F3 [Blocker] ux-browser-review: The remediation preserves image ratios but leaves large gaps between grid rows at 980 and 1280 pixels. At 980, Reading starts 387 pixels below Storytime because Primary determines the row height. At 1280, CodeCamp starts 394 pixels below Storytime in en and zh, and 332 pixels below Storytime in th. The Reading column also has about 588–618 pixels of unused first-row height. These gaps make the program grid unbalanced and extend the section unnecessarily. Evidence: /home/daniebo/.cache/opencode/ux-wfp-r3/en-programs-980.png, en-programs-1280.png, th-programs-1280.png, and en-features-1280-live-1200.png. This defect follows the changed intrinsic image height and self-start classes in commit 71d522662. Route to Green: remove row-dependent gaps with a two-column masonry layout, or place the Primary image beside its text at desktop widths. Preserve the five-card DOM order, approved copy, complete Storytime face, and uncropped 375x622 Primary ratio. Keep automatic card height. Recheck all three widths and locales.

Four completed builds ran through heavy-run in the foreground. Three stopped on the Next.js security notice. The fourth exited 0. A lock wait exceeded one shell timeout before a retry. No upgrade or package change occurred.
Next.js reports a known security vulnerability and recommends a security upgrade. The orchestrator must handle this separately. The browser audit does not authorize an upgrade, push, or deploy.
page-check produced all 18 captures and reports. Every Features viewport shows four loaded photographs, without a hidden, blank, or covered photograph. Pricing intentionally contains no photographs.

The corrected Playwright run inspected all 18 route and viewport combinations with system Chrome. Every route returned HTTP 200 and one h1. Document, body, and page-main widths equal the viewport. No image failed. No console error, page error, or HTTP error appeared.
F1 withdrawn: inspected Storytime at all three widths and locales. At 980, its 366x282 source renders at 460x354.42 pixels. The complete face remains visible without stretching or CSS cropping.
F2 withdrawn: inspected CodeCamp at all three widths and locales. At 980, its height is 181.5 pixels, with 25 pixels below its last text. The previous internal blank area is gone.

F3 differs from F2. F2 concerned blank space inside CodeCamp. F3 concerns gaps outside cards, caused by row sizing beside the taller Primary image. Native section captures and a live viewport confirm F3.
At 980, en and zh Storytime ends at y=1546.45 and Reading starts at y=1933.52. Thai has the same 387.06-pixel gap. The intended grid gap is 24 pixels.
At 1280, en and zh Storytime ends at y=1498.67 and CodeCamp starts at y=1892.17. Primary is 1028.89 pixels tall. Reading is 411.28 pixels tall.
At 1280, Thai Storytime ends at y=1469.42 and CodeCamp starts at y=1801.42. Primary is 967.39 pixels tall. Reading is 379.28 pixels tall.
Viewed all 18 clean captures. The single-column Features layout passes at 390. All Pricing layouts pass. Features fails grid balance at 980 and 1280 in every locale.

Thai headings, body text, cards, FAQ controls, and price cells wrap without clipped text or sideways scrolling. Native Thai section captures support the full-page review. Daniel's Thai wording gate remains separate.
Every 390-pixel price table measures 358 pixels. Each table has a caption, three scoped column headers, five scoped row headers, and five price rows. Values and labels remain readable.
All 54 FAQ checks opened with Enter and closed with Space. Each summary showed the native automatic focus outline. All six additional Tab checks moved from the first summary to the second.

A separate interaction run waited for destination URLs. All 12 CTA clicks reached the locale-specific Tutor or Contact page. The earlier run sampled URLs before client navigation completed; those samples do not prove destination behavior.

All three Features anchor clicks reached #programs. The heading starts at approximately y=79.5 below the mobile header. Live desktop scrolling at y=0, 1200, and 1900 retained one header at top=0 and bottom=81.

The contrast probe checked 58 visible Features elements and 59 visible Pricing elements in each locale at 390 pixels. The minimum measured ratio was 7.30:1. No checked text failed its AA threshold. Screenshot content was not part of this text probe.
Hierarchy, section order, text sizes, labels, and contrast pass outside F3. Optional missing photographs create no empty image boxes, as D7 permits. No additional photograph is required.
The approved images show no staff header, preview banner, or cut face. Primary keeps its 375x622 ratio. Tutor keeps its 520x880 ratio. Reading omits its staff controls.
The zh pages use English body copy with Chinese navigation and footer text, as D4 permits. This audit does not approve Chinese translation quality.

Accessibility snapshots preserve headings, image alternatives, links, table semantics, and disclosure labels. Existing nested main landmarks remain. The price table also repeats its values in a screen-reader summary. This remediation changes neither pattern.
These static pages contain no changed form, data-loading state, empty-data state, or error-recovery action. Normal image loading completed without a broken or empty slot.

One Playwright command failed before browser launch because of a scratch syntax error. The corrected command completed all 18 contexts. A later interaction command exceeded the lock timeout; its foreground retry passed.
Stopped only audit server PID 417504, obtained from ss for port 3123. The final port check shows no listener. No implementation, test, plan, registry, package, or commit changed.

The assigned branch and worktree remain for Green remediation and the later merge gate. Other nondefault branches and worktrees remain with their owning sessions. Daniel's Thai, look, push, and deploy gates remain closed.
